text: Everything from Lessons 3 through 12 is working. Billing's index is in place and maintained on schedule, Scheduling's transaction fix is holding, and the health dashboard has been quiet. Then a new message arrives: the provider-schedule lookup was fine yesterday, and today it's crawling for some providers but not others. Nothing was deployed.

Before guessing at a cause, reproduce the report precisely. Time the procedure for a provider that's reportedly fine and one that's reportedly slow. If both are fast or both are slow, the report describes something else. If one is fast and one is slow, you've confirmed it's real, with two concrete numbers instead of a vague complaint.

Run several more providers through the same timed test. The pattern that emerges: providers with a typical or large number of appointments are slow. One specific provider — a part-time provider with a very small number of appointments — is fast, and always was.

The stored procedure hasn't been edited. That's a real, verifiable fact, but it's not the same as nothing changed. Query plans, cached in the plan cache, can change for reasons that have nothing to do with the procedure's own text — a statistics update, a recompile, or simply which provider happened to be passed in the first time it compiled.

Don't rewrite the procedure yet, and don't assume this is the same missing-index pattern just because it also touches dbo dot Appointments. You have a reproducible symptom and a real pattern, but not yet a confirmed cause. Lesson 14 follows that lead.
